Count and two-part models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_counts.R
table_regression_counts.Rd

table_regression() reads the zero-inflated and hurdle models of pscl::zeroinfl() and pscl::hurdle(). The count coefficients fill the rows, and the zero component follows them as a labeled block of rows in the same columns. The zero-inflation, hurdle and dispersion components of glmmTMB::glmmTMB() render as the same blocks; the other rules of glmmTMB fits, random effects included, are in table_regression_mixed. Poisson and negative-binomial models fitted by glm() or MASS::glm.nb() follow the rules of table_regression(); their dispersion rows are described below.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  show_components = TRUE,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for count models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
zeroinflpscl::zeroinfl()yes (combined response)IRR (count) + OR (logit zero part)Zero-inflationclassical, CR1 (classical only for a negative-binomial part)
hurdlepscl::hurdle()yes (combined response)IRR (count) + OR (logit zero part)Zero hurdleclassical, CR1 (classical only for a negative-binomial part)

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available; the AME of a two-part model is the effect on the overall expected count E(Y). Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Counts, two-part").

What the table shows

Count rows. One row per coefficient of the count component. Under exponentiate = TRUE they are rate ratios of the count process: for zeroinfl, the rate among units not in the structural-zero class; for hurdle, the latent untruncated rate. They are not multiplicative effects on the overall expected count E(Y).

Zero component. Two-part models show their full model, and the note says what each block models:

  • zeroinfl, and glmmTMB with ziformula: a Zero-inflation block, the model for the probability of a structural zero.

  • hurdle: a Zero hurdle, Pr(y > 0) block, the model for the probability of a nonzero count, the opposite direction, hence the distinct label.

  • A glmmTMB hurdle model (a zero-truncated family, ziGamma(), lognormal() or beta_family() with ziformula): a Zero hurdle, Pr(y = 0) block, the probability of a zero.

  • glmmTMB with covariates in dispformula: a Dispersion block, on the log scale, never exponentiated.

The component rows carry Wald inference (B, SE, z, p, CI), join the p_adjust family and take significance stars.

AME. The effect on the overall expected count E(Y), combining the count and zero processes, computed by marginaleffects::avg_slopes() on the full model. The zero-component rows carry no AME of their own, since the combined effect includes them.

Arguments for this family

show_components

Logical. TRUE (default) displays the zero-inflation, zero-hurdle and dispersion components as labeled blocks of rows below the count coefficients. FALSE omits the blocks; the title still names the model type. The argument also governs the Scale effects block of an ordinal::clm() fit (table_regression_ordinal).

The arguments shared with other classes take these values for count models:

exponentiate

Rate ratios for the count rows. A zero component is exponentiated only when its link makes the result an odds ratio (the logit zero components). Probit, cauchit and cloglog zero links, and count-type hurdle zero parts, stay on the link scale, and the note says so.

vcov, cluster

Poisson and geometric zeroinfl and hurdle fits: "classical" and "CR1". A fit with a negative-binomial part: "classical" only. glmmTMB: "classical", "CR0" and "CR1". See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

show_fit_stats

The dispersion rows below.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

The coefficients of both components are tested by Wald z.

"CR1" for Poisson and geometric pscl fits comes from sandwich::vcovCL(), which covers both components at once: the CR0 sandwich scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), G the number of clusters, the one cluster estimator of these classes. A negative-binomial zeroinfl or hurdle keeps its model-based standard errors: the sandwich of these fits leaves out the score of theta. When the count part is negative binomial, fit the model with glmmTMB instead (family nbinom2 with ziformula, or truncated_nbinom2 for a hurdle), whose sandwich includes it; glmmTMB's zero hurdle is binomial, as with zero.dist = "binomial". A hurdle whose zero part alone is negative binomial (zero.dist = "negbin") is refused too; refit it with the default zero.dist = "binomial", which keeps "CR1".

"CR0" and "CR1" for glmmTMB fits come from glmmTMB's own sandwich and cover the zero-inflation and dispersion blocks; see table_regression_mixed.

Fit statistics

The dispersion of a negative-binomial fit is an opt-in fit-statistic row: "theta" and "alpha" (= 1/theta, the Stata nbreg convention) for NB2 fits, among them zeroinfl and hurdle with dist = "negbin", whose theta is that of the count part; "delta" for NB1 fits (glmmTMB nbinom1). A Poisson column in the same table is blank on these rows. See Vocabulary tokens in table_regression() for the classes each token covers.

What is refused, and why

  • HC*: the pscl fits have no hat values, so the HC machinery of sandwich fails on them.

  • A robust vcov for a pscl fit with a negative-binomial part (see above).

  • "CR0", "CR2", "CR3", "bootstrap" and "jackknife" for the pscl fits: "CR1" is their one robust estimator.

  • standardized, for zeroinfl and hurdle.

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; table_regression_mixed for glmmTMB fits; the Count and two-part regression tables article.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit <- pscl::zeroinfl(art ~ fem + kid5 | kid5, data = bioChemists)
  print(table_regression(fit, exponentiate = TRUE))

  # Count rows only.
  print(table_regression(fit, show_components = FALSE))
}
